sources.entry: KextViewer - View all modules on that are loaded in the OS kernel. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/objective-see/KextViewr)

summary.name: KextViewr
summary.one_liner: KextViewr is a macOS utility that displays all currently loaded kernel modules (kexts) in a searchable, filterable UI and can export the list as JSON.
use_cases: Inspect which kernel extensions are loaded on a Mac
Filter out Apple kexts to see only third-party kernel modules
Export loaded kernel module list as JSON
Check kext collection, size, address and architecture
Search kernel modules by name or path
summary.what_it_does: KextViewr lists every loaded kernel module, including Apple's own, with its name, bundle ID, full path, collection (boot, system, or auxiliary), address, size and architecture. A search box filters rows by name or path, and hashtag filters such as #apple and #nonapple narrow the list to system or third-party modules. A checkbox hides Apple-signed kexts. Buttons let the user reload the list and save the results as JSON. It gets its data by calling Apple's kmutil tool, which holds the entitlement needed to read kext info.
notable: Uses Apple's kmutil tool, which has the entitlement third-party apps cannot get
caveats: Requires macOS 11 or later; older macOS versions need the legacy 1.1.0 release
Only shows kexts that kmutil/kextstat reports, so hidden or rootkit kernel modules may not appear
